analysis.label: misaligned
analysis.reason: The paper restricts adversaries to probabilistic polynomial time (PPT), but the formal tSdhAssumption quantifies all functions of the relevant Lean type. An unrestricted function can recover τ from g₂^τ in the SRS and win the t-SDH experiment with probability 1, making the hardness premise false when error<1 and departing from the paper's computational-hardness assumption.

semantic_argument: Section 2 restricts adversaries to algorithms that are PPT in the security parameter. The current tSdhAssumption quantifies all functions of type tSdhAdversary, without a resource bound or model-class restriction.
The root premise pairing(g₁,g₂)≠0 implies g₂≠1. In a prime-order group, nonidentity g₂ generates the group, so τ↦g₂^τ is injective on ZMod p.
The second verifier-group element in the SRS contains g₂^τ. A Lean function with no computational-resource restriction can recover τ using the inverse of this exponentiation map.
The adversary outputs (c,h)=(1-τ,g₁). Since τ+c=1≠0 and g₁^(1/(τ+c))=g₁, tSdhCondition holds for every sampled τ, giving success probability 1.
Thus the formal hardness assumption has no instance when error<1. When error≥1, the probability bound has no nontrivial security content. This is not the PPT hardness condition used in the paper.

corroboration.role: The after source in the same before/after pair contains a Lean proof that the unrestricted-class assumption fails when error<1. This review only read the proof and checked the definitions; it did not recompile them.

limitations: The negative label concerns the adversary-class mismatch in the hardness premise; it does not claim that the Lean implication theorem with that premise is false.
An unbounded inverse function is not a PPT attack; it does not establish a break of the paper's cryptographic assumption.
This decision does not change the aligned label for kzg-binding-after or propagate to reduction roots without a hardness assumption.
Retain the existing provisional-label convention and evaluation_eligible=false, without automatically promoting the record to a human gold label.
